title: Your Fridge Is 5 Degrees Too Warm
sendTrigger: Save this for your next fridge clean-out.
editorialNotes: The brief draws a "$300-500/yr in spoilage" label in its slide 1 visual notes; it is not slide copy and is deliberately not carried (unsourced).
Shelf-life gains (milk 5-7 vs 7-10 days etc.) are the brief's own figures with only an FDA/USDA general citation.

copy.headline: Your fridge is probably set to 40°F.
Your milk isn't dying of old age. It's dying of heat.
The FDA says "40°F or below." The "or below" is doing all the work.
copy.citation: FDA Food Code; USDA Food Safety guidelines.

copy.headline: Most fridges show a 1-5 dial, not degrees.
copy.body: You have no idea what temperature you're at. The factory set it. You never touched it. Neither did the last owner.

copy.headline: Milk at 40°F lasts 5-7 days. At 37°F: 7-10.
copy.body: One dial adjustment, made once, extends everything.

copy.headline: The fix: buy a fridge thermometer ($5-10).
The cheapest way to extend every single item in your fridge: turn the dial down.
Three degrees buys you days.
